item.description: arXiv:2610.11453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) operating in the visible spectral range are crucial for quantum technologies, optical sensing, and nonlinear optics applications. However, their development is hampered by limited integration density and operational bandwidth, linked to low refractive index contrast and restricted parameter space in intuition-based PIC design. item.description: arXiv:2610.11940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reveal temporal chirality in time-modulated photonic media: reversing the orientation of a closed loop traced by the complex permittivity can leave the Floquet spectrum unchanged while strongly modifying the directional scattering response under the same excitation. item.description: arXiv:2610.12062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust corner states have attracted considerable attention in recent years, particularly in photonic systems. They are typically realized in second-order topological insulators, including shrunken-expanded lattices and breathing Kagome lattices, where global symmetries are essential in their formation. item.title: One quantum material, two superconducting states: Stretching helps explain conflicting experiments
item.description: Unconventional superconductors can host unusual electronic states, but understanding what drives their superconductivity becomes difficult when different forms of order coexist. The kagome metal CsV3Sb5 has become a particularly debated example.

item.title: Heavy fermions emerge at an atomic-layer interface, unlocking new ways to design quantum materials
item.description: A research team led by the University of Osaka has directly observed, for the first time, an unusual heavy-fermion state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. Such states are closely linked to exotic quantum phenomena, including unconventional superconductivity, and the finding opens new possibilities for designing quantum materials through their interfaces.

item.title: From Solid-State Spin Defects to Fluorescent Proteins: A Perspective on Quantum Optical Sensing Platforms for Biomedical Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.11644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum optical sensing has evolved from isolated solid state spin defect platforms to increasingly bio-integrated systems designed for biomedical applications. item.title: Photoluminescence study of Vanadium in 4H- and 6H- Silicon Carbide
item.description: arXiv:2610.10781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Point defects with optically addressable spin states are a key building block for quantum networks, but few solid-state emitters combine a spin-photon interface with emission in the low-loss telecommunications band. item.description: arXiv:2610.11178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report an accurate optical frequency synthesizer, which can generate single-frequency laser light with high frequency stability and accuracy at desired frequencies over a wide optical region. item.description: arXiv:2610.11274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional diffractive deep neural networks (D2NNs) treat polarization as independent channels and rely on scalar or semi-vectorial propagation models, which neglect cross polarization coupling and vector diffraction. Here we propose a vector D2NN (V-D2NN) that embeds the full vector angular spectrum method into the end-to-end training pipeline. item.description: arXiv:2610.11420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical sub-diffraction imaging has become an essential tool in modern research. Recently, a new imaging strategy has been demonstrated that exploits the strongly nonlinear excitation-emission response of rare-earth-doped nanocrystals operating in the photon avalanche (PA) regime. item.title: Simulations of Fluorescence and Energy Transfer in Periodic Systems: Pitfalls and Considerations for Bound States in the Continuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.11457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) combine high quality factors with strong electromagnetic-field localization and are therefore widely explored for enhancing light--matter interactions. However, large field amplitudes do not directly translate into useful fluorescence enhancement or energy transfer enhancement between two donor--acceptor fluorophores. item.title: Learning qBIC Resonances across Metasurface Families in Dielectric Fourier Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.11500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BIC) metasurfaces are typically described by geometry-specific parameters, hindering cross-geometry comparison, while ultranarrow qBIC features are easily diluted in full-spectrum learning. Here, 2015 samples from seven dielectric metasurface families are mapped to a shared reciprocal-lattice grid, where two frozen low-order Fourier channels capture resonance shifts with mean within-branch $R^2$ values of 0.871-0.999.

item.title: Minimizing round-trip loss for near-unity quantum efficiency in organic light-emitting diodes
item.description: arXiv:2610.12065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) reach internal quantum efficiencies close to 100%, yet in a planar device only 20-30% of photons escape. item.description: arXiv:2610.12146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultrafast science is rapidly evolving from a collection of specialized laser experiments into a facility-scale, data-intensive research endeavour. item.title: Structured leakage in OAM-encoded qubits revealed by distributed quantum feature extraction
item.description: arXiv:2610.11001v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes have emerged as an important platform for high-dimensional quantum communication but remain vulnerable to environmental noise and channel imperfections. Here we introduce a logical-qubit representation of OAM propagation in which modes evolve as qubits through noisy quantum channels. item.description: arXiv:2610.11698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extracting spectral properties such as energy position, broadening, and spectral weight from dielectric spectra is critical for interpreting collective electronic excitations in many-body physics. item.title: Local polarization control of optical tweezer arrays
item.description: arXiv:2610.12406v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical tweezer arrays trapping ultracold atoms and molecules are a versatile quantum science platform with broad impact in quantum simulation, quantum computation, and quantum metrology. item.title: SHINE lights up the extremes
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02017-8 The Shanghai High Repetition Rate XFEL and Extreme Light Facility is approaching its first lasing. Nature Photonics spoke with Zhentang Zhao, director of the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility and the SHINE project, about the facility’s capabilities and future plans.

item.title: Delaying light from quantum dots
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02015-w Förster energy transfer can prolong the photoluminescence decay of a receiving colloidal quantum dot, revealing a possible route to optically control recombination in nanocrystal assemblies.

item.title: Time-stretch spectroscopy breaks temporal aliasing barrier
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02006-x A temporally super-resolved single-shot method overcomes the long-standing temporal–spectral trade-off in time-stretch spectroscopy. The outcome is continuous measurements of non-repetitive spectral dynamics with picosecond resolution, providing a three-orders-of-magnitude improvement over the current state of the art.

item.title: Optomechanics for piconewton force metrology
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02011-0 Of the sensors that can directly sense forces in the pico- and sub-pico-newton ranges, only a few can measure in liquids. Microfibre-based microcantilevers now add to this family, providing a versatile, broad-bandwidth, high-sensitivity optomechanical sensor.

item.title: Hybrid nanophotonic trap boosts atomic storage and coherence times
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02005-y A hybrid nanophotonic trap that replaces the attractive red-detuned laser field with atom–surface interactions — Casimir–Polder interactions and electrostatic attraction — achieves record-long storage and coherence times for cold atoms coupled to a nanofibre surface.

item.title: Gravity and light reveal how liquids turn into thin fibers
item.description: From spiders spinning their webs to the manufacturing of textiles, the formation of fibers from liquids plays an important role in both nature and industry. Yet accurately predicting the properties of such fibers remains a challenge. The fiber is often much thinner than the nozzle from which a polymer or solution is extruded. Factors such as temperature, flow conditions and chemical reactions ultimately determine a fiber's thickness and strength.

item.title: Levitating glass sphere becomes entangled with light at room temperature
item.description: Today, many physicists are actively exploring how light could be used to link objects through quantum entanglement. By fully harnessing the effect, they hope to unlock a wide array of applications, from secure communication networks spanning vast distances to sensitive new tests of the fundamental laws of physics.
